chapter_title: Chương 46: 0046【Tật Ngoài Da, Không Giá Trị】

segments.title: Chương 46: 0046【Tật Ngoài Da, Không Giá Trị】
segments.content:
Shanda Headquarters.

Wednesday, the sixth day since Abyss Legend went online.

"Director Zhang, the technical department refuses to engage in hacking."

"What do they mean?"

"Director Chen said their main responsibilities are cybersecurity maintenance and technical R&D. They're currently overloaded with work and can't spare the manpower for hacking."

"I understand."

Zhang Yingfeng, the head of legal affairs and copyright, was currently feeling a bit angry.

He was busy arranging manpower to investigate real-world infringing manufacturers and hadn't paid any attention to the private server issue at all.

When he received the report about Abyss Legend two days ago, Zhang Yingfeng hadn't thought much of it and had casually signed off on authorizing a hacking attack.

But when it went through the procedures to the technical department, it was actually rejected.

Zhang Yingfeng couldn't even get angry about it, because the head of the technical department was Boss Chen's own younger brother, one of Shanda's founders.

For now, let's call him Chen Xiaodi.

Shanda's acquisition of Qidian Chinese Network was personally masterminded by Chen Xiaodi.

At this time, Shanda had a president, a vice president, and a large group of department directors.

The president was naturally Boss Chen.

The vice president, Zhu William, was originally the founder of Rongshu Xia. He was poached by Boss Chen half a year ago to improve the internal structure, handle external acquisitions and expansion, and concurrently liaise with Wall Street to pursue a public listing.

As for Chen Xiaodi, he was at the director level.

Zhang Yingfeng worked to calm his emotions. Only after ensuring there was not a trace of anger in his voice did he personally go to speak with Chen Xiaodi.

"Knock, knock, knock!"

"Come in."

Chen Xiaodi was wearing a pair of half-rimmed glasses, a T-shirt with jeans, and a sweater over them. There was even a bed in his office; he often worked until midnight and then just slept at the company.

"Director Chen." Zhang Yingfeng greeted with a smile.

Chen Xiaodi's fingers flew across the keyboard. Without looking up, he said, "Have a seat."

Zhang Yingfeng sat down across the desk, and a secretary brought him a cup of coffee.

"What's the matter?" Chen Xiaodi asked.

Zhang Yingfeng organized his thoughts and said in the calmest tone possible, "Director Chen, it's like this. A private server has recently appeared and its impact has been very negative. I need to deploy a few hackers."

Chen Xiaodi was always direct: "I know about Abyss Legend. Its player count is lower than Dudu Legend's. We don't even need hackers for Dudu Legend, so why are you attacking Abyss Legend?"

"The impact on public opinion is extremely detrimental. They're even coming into Legend to poach our players," Zhang Yingfeng said.

Chen Xiaodi said, "Aren't you supposed to be cooperating with the five ministries' special crackdown? Just take down the private server platforms. From the end of last year until now, why hasn't the company used hackers to attack private servers anymore? Besides the fact that there are too many to fight, hacking brings serious negative consequences for the company!"

"Director Chen, I'm just doing my job. I hope you can understand," Zhang Yingfeng said.

"I can't understand," Chen Xiaodi retorted. "I'm in charge of technology, and I was against using hackers last year. This thing is a double-edged sword; use it too much and you'll end up cutting yourself. If you resort to hacking for every little thing, then what do we have a legal department for?"

Private servers weren't illegal, but hacking was. Ever since Shanda used hackers at the end of 2002, they had been very cautious with this sort of thing.

A few years later, although they started using hackers again, they were always reluctant to do it themselves. Instead, they first formed a team (which later became a subsidiary) and used externally hired personnel to go undercover in various private servers. Those hacking teams were also formed by external hires and had no direct connection to Shanda itself.

There really was no connection, to the point that Shanda even lost control.

One of the external hires colluded with a member of Shanda's anti-private-server team to directly collect protection money from the private servers on the market. Servers that paid the protection fee could survive, while those that didn't were cracked down upon severely.

Eventually, they set their sights on the private server platforms, using hacking as a threat against any that disobeyed. Gradually, the largest private server platforms in the country all had to listen to Shanda's external hires...

Shanda chose to report it to the police, but even after the people were arrested, they were only fined. It was difficult for the relevant authorities to convict them.

In other words, aside from when private servers first appeared, when Shanda did use hacking attacks, for the next twenty-plus years, no matter how rampant private servers became, Shanda never again directly employed hacking as a method.

Zhang Yingfeng explained patiently, "The legislation is currently incomplete, and normal legal means are ineffective, which is why I suggested using hackers."

Chen Xiaodi couldn't be bothered to argue anymore. "If you want to use hackers, that's fine. First, go get my brother's (Boss Chen's) signature."

"Alright, goodbye, Director Chen." Zhang Yingfeng left, bottling up a bellyful of fire.

Chen Xiaodi also took his hands off the keyboard, leaned back in his chair, and closed his eyes to rest.

His education only went up to vocational high school, and he had worked as a cashier after graduation. But he taught himself computer technology, developed China's first internet billing software, and broke Microsoft's monopoly in that field in China.

At the age of 21, he followed his brother to found Shanda and was its second-largest shareholder.

But as things developed, he was on the verge of being squeezed out of the decision-making circle.

This wasn't some fraternal falling-out. Rather, aside from being decent at technology, Chen Xiaodi was really lacking in other areas and had been publicly criticized by his brother more than once.

In the future, he would only be in charge of two areas:

One was Shanda Literature, which included a whole host of literary websites like Qidian, Jinjiang, Rongshu Xia, Hongxiu Tianxiang, Xiaoxiang Shuyuan, and Xiaoshuo Yuedu Wang.

The other was the Shanda Innovation Institute, becoming a pioneer in fields like cloud computing and voice input in China. He was the first person in China to develop cloud computing.

On the seventh day of Abyss Legend's launch, Boss Chen finally flew back to the Magic City.

On this trip, he not only went to Beijing for meetings but was also received by high-level leaders to discuss the development of China's online gaming industry. Afterwards, he exchanged opinions with other game companies and also visited some tech companies in the capital.

A trivial matter like a private server had long been cast to the back of Boss Chen's mind.

As soon as Boss Chen returned to the company, Vice President Zhu William came to his office. "The acquisition of ZONA has been settled. We can officially sign next month."

"As expected, you work quickly and reliably," Boss Chen said happily.

ZONA was an American company that possessed world-class game engine development technology.

Shanda was buying ZONA, naturally, to enhance its own R&D capabilities!

Boss Chen asked, "How did your meeting with Wall Street go on this trip to America?"

Zhu William said, "I contacted a few old friends, and they're very interested in Shanda. If President Chen wants to list on the NASDAQ, it would be best to find an industry insider to be specifically in charge of that."

"What do you think of Tang Jun?" Boss Chen asked.

"Which Tang Jun?" Zhu William said.

Boss Chen said, "Microsoft's person-in-charge here in Shanghai."

Zhu William answered honestly, "I don't know the man, so I can't comment."

Boss Chen added, "If Tang Jun comes, he will take over all of your current duties."

This was to take away all of Zhu William's existing authority.

Zhu William smiled without a word.

Boss Chen continued, "After Tang Jun is onboard, I'll give you Shanda Xinhua."

"What does President Chen want?" Zhu William asked.

Boss Chen said, "Shanda Xinhua has been established for half a year without much progress. I need you to go and break new ground, to integrate the merchandise for all of Shanda's products. And build up a formidable tech team to be responsible for R&D in computer software, hardware, and network technology. You also need to build up investment and marketing teams to acquire promising enterprises. You must strive for Shanda's diversified and technological development. Shanda's future is in your hands. You can also take some of the technical staff from headquarters with you."

"About Director Chen..." Zhu William didn't want to usurp the power of the company's second-largest shareholder and the president's own brother.

How could an outsider meddle in the affairs between brothers?

Boss Chen said, "I will personally persuade my brother."

Zhu William no longer refused, but he set a condition: "If I go to Shanda Xinhua, I want sufficient authority."

"From finance to management, you will be in sole charge. You won't need to report to me. Just treat Shanda Xinhua as your own company." Boss Chen granted him maximum authority.

"I will do my utmost." Zhu William left after saying his piece.

A scholar dies for a patron who recognizes his worth.

Zhu William's new assignment truly had a hint of him working himself to the bone.

In nine months, he would increase Shanda Xinhua's profits by 18 times and build formidable investment, marketing, and tech teams.

But he would also tire himself to the point of suffering two stomach hemorrhages and proactively resign.

His resignation was so sudden, and he refused to change his mind no matter how they tried to keep him, that Boss Chen couldn't find a qualified successor for a very long time.

Zhu William had just left when Zhang Yingfeng came in.

"We have already confirmed seven locations for the pirate factories and dens," Zhang Yingfeng reported. "We're just waiting for the special operation to begin, and we will immediately provide the leads to the relevant departments. There's also a gang that forges and sells point cards, which we've been monitoring for over two months."

Boss Chen praised, "Well done."

Zhang Yingfeng hesitated for a moment. "There's a Legend private server that's been causing quite a stir. I was hoping to use a hacking attack."

"Just coordinate with the technical department," Boss Chen said.

Zhang Yingfeng said hesitantly, "Director Chen... won't approve the use of hackers."

Hearing this, Boss Chen fell silent.

Zhang Yingfeng felt quite anxious and steeled himself to say, "Director Chen said that if he has your signature, he will agree to carry it out."

Boss Chen pondered for a long time before finally speaking, "He has a point. Hacking is, after all, not a respectable method."

"Then..." Zhang Yingfeng was dumbfounded.

Boss Chen had been consistently weakening his brother's power; for a small matter like this, he had to give his brother enough face.

Sigh, this brother of his was sometimes very obedient, and other times very stubborn.

Just like a child who hadn't grown up.

And he really wasn't old. Chen Xiaodi was only 25 this year, yet he was already Shanda's second-largest shareholder and third most powerful figure!

He had to be suppressed, yet also placated.

Boss Chen said, "You don't need to worry about that private server. Stick to the original plan and focus on cracking down on the private server platforms."

Zhang Yingfeng tried to make his case one more time. "That private server's impact is very detrimental."

"Is its scale very large?" Boss Chen asked.

Zhang Yingfeng said, "The scale isn't the largest. Its player count is lower than Dudu Legend's. But its impact on public opinion is terrible; it even made it onto the homepage news of 17173."

Boss Chen finally showed some interest. "How did they manage that?"

Zhang Yingfeng said, "A series of posts guided public opinion, stirring up players' resentment toward Shanda. Even netizens from Tianya and Xici Hutong joined in on the commotion."

"Is that the one that posted the 'game refugee post'?" Boss Chen asked.

Zhang Yingfeng said, "That's the one. It's called Abyss Legend."

Boss Chen logged onto the 17173 forums, briefly looked through those few posts, and surprisingly exclaimed with admiration, "These people really know their way around publicity. What is their Abyss Map like?"

"They just copy maps that have a boss, sell tickets to a copied version, and let one team have exclusive access to a map. And they only copy the level where the boss is located," Zhang Yingfeng said.

Boss Chen thought for a moment. "We could add an Abyss Map feature to the Age of Heroes we're currently developing."

Zhang Yingfeng said, "Age of Heroes sells point cards. That conflicts with charging for map tickets."

"Have the development team study how to integrate it," Boss Chen said.

Zhang Yingfeng asked, "Are we really not going to take down this private server?"

Boss Chen sighed and said, "You can't catch all the rats. Your job is to clean out the rats' nest."

To Chen Guiliang and Tao Chenggang, Abyss Legend was a big deal.

But in Boss Chen's eyes, it was truly just a small matter. When he saw the post half a month ago, he was just curious about Chen Guiliang's methods. Now that the mystery was solved, he was no longer interested.

Recruit them?

Impossible.

If they brought the private server team over, what positions should they be given? What salary should they be offered?

Those guys were already making money running a private server. If the salary was too low, why would they be willing to be recruited? If the salary was high and the position senior, what would Shanda's other employees think?

Besides, at this moment, Shanda was already developing two new games and had no short-term need to start a third.

Resources were limited, after all.

The R&D team for Shanda's Age of Heroes was poached by Boss Shi precisely because a conflict erupted when they couldn't get enough resources.

As for Abyss Legend's instance dungeon gameplay, it conflicted with the official Legend's sale of point cards. Although it had a novel selling point for now, it wasn't profitable in the long run, falling far short of the profits provided by Legend's point cards.

Even if they wanted to borrow the instance dungeon idea, they could just take it and use it for free!

Chen Guiliang and Abyss Legend were of no value to Shanda. They didn't even have enough value to warrant the use of hackers.

Over on Chen Guiliang's side, the monthly exams were fast approaching.

They hadn't even received a cease-and-desist letter from Shanda, nor had any Shanda employees called them or sent them a QQ message.

This, on the contrary, made Chen Guiliang suspicious and paranoid. He called Tao Chenggang every day at noon. "Brother Gang, still no movement from Shanda?"

Tao Chenggang was also baffled. "Yeah, we've already opened the tenth server, and the first few servers are about to be merged. Why the hell is there still no word from Shanda? They're not planning something big, are they? I'm worried the police will suddenly show up at my door."

"Uh... let's just wait and see. Even if we get caught, it'll just be a fine, and a few days in detention at most," Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Chenggang said, feeling apprehensive, "I'm going to consult a lawyer again."
